King Solomon. The son and successor of King David, renowned for his wisdom, wealth, and architectural grandeur.

Born to David and Bathsheba after the death of their first child, representing redemption from their tragic sin, Solomon presided over Israel at the height of its power and prosperity. When God offered him any blessing, he chose wisdom above all else, asking for insight and understanding to judge his people rightly, which pleased God.

He built the First Temple in Jerusalem, a magnificent structure that housed the Ark of the Covenant and became the center of Israelite worship and sacrifice. He was famed for his wealth, receiving tribute from surrounding nations, and his extensive trade networks made Israel prosperous. He composed thousands of proverbs and songs, with traditions attributing the book of Proverbs and Ecclesiastes to his authorship.

He had many wives, tradition says seven hundred, and many children, though this multiplicity of relationships also drew him toward foreign gods and idolatry. Though he inherited a united and stable kingdom, his heavy taxation and complex politics would sow seeds of division after his death. His reign marked the apex of Israel's unified power; the kingdom would divide after his death into northern Israel and southern Judah. His life is recorded in First Kings chapters one through eleven and Second Chronicles chapters one through nine.
